Food presets Brands Chart Guide EN English Español Português Français Deutsch Why frozen food converts differently Most converters treat frozen as one more food type and apply the usual rule: take 25°F off and cut the time by a fifth. That is backwards for food straight from the freezer. The pack's oven instructions were written for food that goes in frozen, so the temperature on the box is already the one the coating needs to crisp before the inside overcooks. What the air fryer changes is speed: a small cavity and fast air drive the ice out of the surface quickly. So this converter keeps most of the pack temperature — usually 10°F off — and takes the big cut on time, around 30%. Raw frozen chicken is the exception and goes lower and slower. Reading a UK pack vs. a US pack US packs give one oven temperature in °F, written for a conventional oven. UK and European packs usually give °C and often two numbers: a conventional temperature and a lower "fan" temperature, typically 20°C apart, with the same time for both. Pick the line you are reading from with the pack toggle. A fan temperature is already fan-adjusted, so the converter adds back the gap between conventional and fan cooking for that food instead of cutting again — the same per-food gap the convection converter uses. Gas mark packs are conventional: convert the mark to a temperature first, or use the gas mark shown under each result to check you are close. Worked example A US bag of frozen fries says 425°F for 20 minutes. A basket air fryer tops out at 400°F, so the converter holds it there and adds a little time back: 400°F for 15 minutes, with two shakes. A UK bag of the same fries reads 200°C fan for 20 minutes; with the fan toggle that becomes 400°F (205°C) for 13 minutes — slightly shorter, because it no longer needs the time the ceiling clamp added back. Don't overcrowd the basket Frozen food releases water as it thaws, and in a full basket that water has nowhere to go. Pieces stacked on each other steam instead of crisping, and the bottom layer stays pale however long you cook it. Keep fries, nuggets, and wings to one layer, or close to it, and cook a large bag in two batches — the second batch is usually a minute or two faster because the basket is already hot. The shake times in the result break up pieces frozen together and turn the bottom layer up into the air. Raw chicken from frozen Raw frozen breasts, wings, and many breaded chicken products have to reach 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part, not just look brown. These get a smaller time cut and a lower temperature so the center catches up with the outside, and the result shows a reminder to check with a thermometer. Fully cooked products, like most nuggets, only need heating through, so they show the target without the warning. Keep the pack temperature or take about 10°F off, cut the time by around 30%, and shake or flip at the marks the converter shows. If the pack temperature is above what your air fryer can reach, the converter holds it at the maximum and adds a little time back. How long do frozen fries take in an air fryer? Usually 12–16 minutes at 400°F for a standard bag that says 425°F for 20 minutes in the oven, shaken twice. Thick-cut fries take longer than shoestring. Enter your pack numbers above for the exact setting. How long does frozen raw chicken take in an air fryer? Longer than you would expect from the 30% rule. Raw frozen breast cooks at a lower temperature with only about 15% off the pack time, so the center reaches 165°F before the outside dries. Always check with a thermometer. Should I thaw frozen food before air frying? No. Pack instructions and this converter both assume the food goes in frozen. Thawing first makes coatings soggy and changes the timing. The exception is a large raw roast, which should be thawed in the fridge. My pack gives a fan oven temperature. Which one do I enter? Either works — just set the pack toggle to match. If you enter the fan temperature, choose "Fan oven" and the converter adds back the right amount for that food. Do I need to preheat the air fryer for frozen food? A short preheat gives more even browning (a few minutes in a basket, longer at higher temperatures; oven-style units preheat on their own) on fries and breaded food. Frozen pizza and reheated items do fine without one. mainEntity.name: How do I convert frozen packaging instructions to an air fryer?
